facts.text: Ashford Castle is surrounded by a 350-acre estate of gardens, forests and woodland overlooking the shores of Lough Corrib in County Mayo.
facts.excerpt: Ashford Castle is surrounded by 350-acres of beautiful manicured gardens, verdant forests and woodland rich with birdlife, all overlooking the shores of rippling Lough Corrib in County Mayo, Ireland.

facts.text: Ashford Castle was once home to the Guinness family.
facts.excerpt: Once home to the Guinness family and today a multi-generational resort

facts.text: Ashford Castle is part of The Red Carnation Hotel Collection.
facts.excerpt: Now a proud part of The Red Carnation Hotel Collection

facts.text: Accommodation includes the historic Boathouse, perched over the lake.
facts.excerpt: including the historic Boathouse, perched over the lake, where couples can hideout in splendid isolation

facts.text: The Boathouse sits on the edge of Lough Corrib and has lake views and a fireplace.
facts.excerpt: The Boathouse offers a secluded, luxurious retreat on the edge of Lough Corrib. Perfect for a romantic escape, it features stunning lake views, a cosy fireplace, and exclusive amenities.

facts.text: Deluxe Queen Family Rooms have two queen size beds overlooking Lough Corrib, with interconnecting rooms available.
facts.excerpt: Our family rooms consist of two queen size beds overlooking Lough Corrib.

facts.text: Fine dining is served in the George V Dining Room, where breakfast is also served daily.
facts.excerpt: Served daily in the George V Dining Room, breakfast at Ashford Castle is a real occasion.

facts.text: The Dungeon serves grill classics.
facts.excerpt: Grill classics amongst medieval grandeur.

facts.text: Afternoon Tea is served in the Connaught Room.
facts.excerpt: a delightful Afternoon Tea in the elegant Connaught Room

facts.text: Squire Danagher's is a private dining experience in the original house where The Quiet Man was filmed in the 1950s, with traditional Irish entertainment.
facts.excerpt: A private dining experience set in the original house where ‘The Quiet Man’ was filmed in the 1950s. Experience traditional Irish entertainment and a hearty local menu in our recently restored cottage.

facts.text: The castle's wine cellar is kept in its secret passageways.
facts.excerpt: alongside an extensive wine cellar kept in the castle's secret passageways

facts.text: Cuisine uses produce foraged from the grounds and grown in the Kitchen Garden.
facts.excerpt: the produce foraged from our grounds and grown in our productive Kitchen Garden

facts.text: The Spa was named Ireland's Best Hotel Spa for the 10th consecutive year at the 2025 World Spa Awards.
facts.excerpt: The Spa at Ashford Castle earned the title of 'Ireland’s Best Hotel Spa' for its 10th consecutive year in the 2025 World Spa Awards

facts.text: The Spa is Ireland's first Forbes Five-Star Spa.
facts.excerpt: proudly holds the distinction of being Ireland's first Forbes Five-Star Spa

facts.text: The Spa has a 'Tree of Life' mural stretching the length of the relaxation pool.
facts.excerpt: a mesmerising 'Tree of Life' mural stretching the length of the relaxation pool

facts.text: Spa facilities include a relaxation pool, a Hammam, a steam room and a fitness suite.
facts.excerpt: The Salon, relaxation pool, five exceptional treatment rooms, an invigorating Hammam, a relaxing steam room, fitness suite, and our serene terrace

facts.text: Guests can try falconry with the estate's experts, with no previous experience necessary.
facts.excerpt: At Ashford Castle, try out the ancient art of Falconry with our experts. No previous experience necessary.

facts.text: The estate has a 9-hole parkland golf course.
facts.excerpt: Our picturesque 9 hole, 2996 yards par 35 parkland course is perfect for golfers of all abilities.

facts.text: Estate activities include horse riding, fishing, falconry, shooting, golf and cycling.
facts.excerpt: from country classic pastimes such as horse riding, fishing, falconry and shooting, to more modern activities such as golf and cycling

facts.text: Complimentary guided walks of the estate are available exclusively for residents.
facts.excerpt: Explore, learn & connect with the estate on guided walks, available exclusively for Ashford Castle residents.

facts.text: Guests can play on two all-weather tennis courts free of charge.
facts.excerpt: We offer guests two newly resurfaced all-weather courts for complimentary play.

facts.text: The castle has a cinema room.
facts.excerpt: Our premier cinema room is a magnificent feature of the castle

facts.text: Canoeing tours on Lough Corrib run from May to September with a local guide.
facts.excerpt: Experience Lough Corrib through Ashford Castle’s private canoeing tour with a professional local guide.

facts.text: Activities are provided by independent companies and contractors, and advance bookings are recommended.
facts.excerpt: All the above mentioned activities are provided and organised by independent companies and contractors and are booked at your own risk. Advance bookings are recommended

facts.text: No swimming is permitted in the lake, river or fountains.
facts.excerpt: No diving, paddling or swimming is permitted in the lake, river or fountains.

facts.text: Ashford Castle is 27 miles from Galway city and 40 miles from Knock.
facts.excerpt: Directions from Galway city (27 miles) Directions from Knock (40 miles)

facts.text: Ashford Castle is 155 miles from Dublin.
facts.excerpt: Directions from Dublin (155 miles)

facts.text: Chauffeured car journeys are available to all major Irish airports.
facts.excerpt: Chauffeured car journeys are available to all major Irish airports.

facts.text: Ashford Castle is in Cong, County Mayo.
facts.excerpt: Cong, County Mayo, Ireland, F31 CA48

facts.text: The castle's spaces were restored in a five-year restoration project using the expertise of local artisans and craftspeople.
facts.excerpt: following our five-year restoration project. The centuries-old expertise of local artisans and craftspeople was central to our restoration project

facts.text: Condé Nast Traveler says the castle has been around since 1228.
facts.excerpt: Ashford Castle, overlooking Lough (lake) Corrib in the Irish county of Mayo, has been around since the year 1228

facts.text: Condé Nast Traveler says the spa is in a bronze former conservatory.
facts.excerpt: the spa, which is located in a bronze former conservatory

facts.text: The Boutique stocks Irish art, clothing and jewellery handcrafted by local partners.
facts.excerpt: The Boutique stocks a collection of the finest Irish art, clothing and jewellery, hand crafted by trusted local partners such as master jeweller, Nigel O'Reilly

facts.text: The Wine Cellar offers guided wine tastings.
facts.excerpt: Guided wine tastings from 12pm to 5.30pm.

facts.text: The hotel describes itself as a Forbes Five-Star hotel.
facts.excerpt: the grand stone gates of our Forbes Five-Star hotel

facts.text: Room count stated as 83 rooms, suites and The Boathouse.
facts.excerpt: Each of the 83 rooms, suites and The Boathouse at Ashford Castle represent traditional elegance and finesse.

facts.excerpt: to the already-luxurious 82-room property
